sanskrit: viṣṇoḥ kramo 'si sapatnahā pṛthivīsaṃśito 'gnitejāḥ | pṛthivīm anu vi krame 'haṃ pṛthivyās taṃ nir bhajāmo yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ | pūrvajān sapatnān avainān bādhe aty enān kramāmy apāṅ apanuttaḥ sapatnaḥ ||
english: You are the stride of Viṣṇu, slayer of rivals, whetted by the Earth, radiant with the fire of Agni. Along the Earth do I stride wide; from the Earth we expel him who hates us and whom we hate. The rivals born before — I press those very ones down; I stride beyond them — driven away and expelled is the rival.

sanskrit: viṣṇoḥ kramo 'si sapatnahā- -antarikṣasaṃśito vāyutejāḥ | antarikṣam anu vi krame 'ham antarikṣāt taṃ nir bhajāmo yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ | sahajān sapatnān (…) ||
english: You are the stride of Viṣṇu, slayer of rivals, whetted by the atmosphere, radiant with the wind of Vāyu. Along the atmosphere do I stride wide; from the atmosphere we expel him who hates us and whom we hate. The rivals born together — [I press those very ones down; I stride beyond them — driven away and expelled is the rival].

sanskrit: viṣṇoḥ kramo 'si sapatnahā dyusaṃśitaḥ sūryatejāḥ | divam anu vi krame 'haṃ divas taṃ nir bhajāmo yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ | aparajān sapatnān (…) ||
english: You are the stride of Viṣṇu, slayer of rivals, whetted by the sky, radiant with the light of Sūrya. Along the sky do I stride wide; from the sky we expel him who hates us and whom we hate. The rivals born after — [I press those very ones down; I stride beyond them — driven away and expelled is the rival].

sanskrit: (…) sapatnahā diksaṃśito vātatejāḥ | diśo anu vi krame 'haṃ digbhyas tam (…) ||
english: [You are the stride of Viṣṇu,] slayer of rivals, whetted by the directions, radiant with the power of the wind. Along the directions do I stride wide; from the directions him — [we expel who hates us and whom we hate; I press the rivals down, I stride beyond them — driven away and expelled is the rival].

sanskrit: (…) sapatnahā- -āśāsaṃsito manastejāḥ | āśā anu vi krame 'ham āśābhyas tam (…) ||
english: [You are the stride of Viṣṇu,] slayer of rivals, whetted by the horizons, radiant with the power of the mind. Along the horizons do I stride wide; from the horizons him — [we expel who hates us and whom we hate; I press the rivals down, I stride beyond them — driven away and expelled is the rival].

sanskrit: (…) sapatnahā- -apsaṃsito varuṇatejāḥ | apo anu vi krame 'ham adbhyas tam (…) ||
english: [You are the stride of Viṣṇu,] slayer of rivals, whetted by the waters, radiant with the power of Varuṇa. Along the waters do I stride wide; from the waters him — [we expel who hates us and whom we hate; I press the rivals down, I stride beyond them — driven away and expelled is the rival].

sanskrit: (…) sapatnahā ṛksaṃśitaḥ sāmatejāḥ | ṛco anu vi krame 'haṃ ṛgbhyas tam (…) ||
english: [You are the stride of Viṣṇu,] slayer of rivals, whetted by the Ṛc hymns, radiant with the power of the Sāman. Along the Ṛc hymns do I stride wide; from the Ṛc hymns him — [we expel who hates us and whom we hate; I press the rivals down, I stride beyond them — driven away and expelled is the rival].

sanskrit: (…) sapatnahā yajñasaṃśito brahmatejāḥ | yajñam anu vi krame 'haṃ yajñāt tam (…) ||
english: [You are the stride of Viṣṇu,] slayer of rivals, whetted by the sacrifice, radiant with the power of brahman. Along the sacrifice do I stride wide; from the sacrifice him — [we expel who hates us and whom we hate; I press the rivals down, I stride beyond them — driven away and expelled is the rival].

sanskrit: (…) sapatnahā- -oṣadhīsaṃśitaḥ somatejāḥ | oṣadhīr anu vi krame 'ham oṣadhībhyas tam (…) ||
english: [You are the stride of Viṣṇu,] slayer of rivals, whetted by the plants, radiant with the power of Soma. Along the plants do I stride wide; from the plants him — [we expel who hates us and whom we hate; I press the rivals down, I stride beyond them — driven away and expelled is the rival].

sanskrit: (…) sapatnahā kṛṣisaṃśitaḥ puruṣatejāḥ | kṛṣim anu vi krame 'haṃ kṛṣyās tam (…) ||
english: [You are the stride of Viṣṇu,] slayer of rivals, whetted by tillage, radiant with the power of the Puruṣa. Along the tillage do I stride wide; from the tillage him — [we expel who hates us and whom we hate; I press the rivals down, I stride beyond them — driven away and expelled is the rival].

sanskrit: viṣṇoḥ kramo 'si sapatnahā prāṇasaṃśito 'nnatejāḥ | prāṇam anu vi krame 'haṃ prāṇāt taṃ nirbhajāmo yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ ||
english: You are the stride of Viṣṇu, slayer of rivals, whetted by the breath, radiant with the power of food. Along the breath do I stride wide; from the breath we utterly expel him who hates us and whom we hate.

sanskrit: agamaṃ svar agamaṃ jyotir abhy aṣṭhāṃ viśvāḥ pṛtanā arātīḥ | yo +'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmas tasyedaṃ prāṇam āyur ni veṣṭayāmi- -idam enam adhamaṃ tamo gamayāmi ||
english: I have reached the sun, I have reached the light; I have stood over all hostile armies and foes-without-gift. He who hates us and whom we hate — his breath and life-span I here wind off; I send this man to the lowest darkness.

sanskrit: sūryasyāvṛtam anv āvarte dakṣiṇām anv āvṛtam | diśo jyotiṣmatīr abhi paryāvarte sapta ṛṣīn abhi paryāvarte brahmābhi paryāvarte brāhmaṇān abhi paryāvarte | te me draviṇaṃ yacchantu te me brāhmaṇavarcasam ||
english: I turn back following Sūrya's circuit; I turn back following the southern course. I circle back toward the luminous directions; I circle back toward the Seven Ṛṣis; I circle back toward brahman; I circle back toward the Brāhmaṇas. May they bestow wealth upon me; may they bestow upon me the brilliance of brahman.

sanskrit: yat te 'nnaṃ bhuvaspata ākṣiyati pṛthivīm anu | tasya nas tvaṃ bhuvaspate saṃprayaccha prajāpate | yaṃ vayaṃ mṛgayāmahe taṃ vadhai stṛṇavāmahi ||
english: O Lord of the Earth, whatever food of yours dwells distributed along the Earth — of that, O Lord of the Earth, O Prajāpati, do generously grant us a share. Him whom we hunt down, let us lay low with the slaying blow.

sanskrit: vyātte parameṣṭhino brahmaṇāpīpadāma tam | vaiśvānarasya daṃṣṭrābhyāṃ mṛtyus taṃ samadhād abhi ||
english: Into the open jaws of Parameṣṭhin we have thrust him with brahman's force. Death has fully overtaken him through the fangs of Vaiśvānara.

sanskrit: iyaṃ taṃ psātv āhutiḥ samid devī sahīyasī | rājño varuṇasya bandho 'si so *'mum āmuṣyāyaṇam amuṣyāḥ putram anne prāṇe badhāna ||
english: Let this oblation, the divine kindling-stick of surpassing strength, devour him. You are the bond of King Varuṇa — bind yonder one, the son of that woman, that scion of that lineage, in food and in breath.

sanskrit: apām asmai vajraṃ pra harāmi caturbhṛṣṭiṃ śīrṣabhidyāya vidvān | so asya parvā pra śṛṇātu sarvā tan me devā hy anu jānantu viśve ||
english: Knowingly I hurl against him the four-pointed thunderbolt of the waters to cleave his skull. Let it shatter all his joints — may all the gods take cognisance of this for me.

sanskrit: yad agne tapasā tapa upa prekṣāmahe vayam | priyāḥ śrutasya bhūyāsma- -āyuṣmantaḥ sumedhasaḥ ||
english: O Agni, when we look upon you through your heat and fervent energy, may we be dear to the Renowned One — long-lived and of keen wisdom.

sanskrit: virāḍ vā idam agre 'jāyata tasyā jātāyā abibhet sarvam | iyam evedaṃ bhaviṣyati na vayam iti ||
english: Verily, Virāj was born first here. When she was born, all things were afraid, thinking: 'This one alone will become all this; not we.'

sanskrit: sod akrāmat sā dakṣiṇāgnau ny akrāmat | yajñarto vāsateyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: She then stepped forth; she descended into the Dakṣiṇāgni. He who knows this becomes fit for sacrifice, a dweller in the abode.

sanskrit: (…) sā gārhapatye ny akrāmat | gṛhamedhī gṛhapatir bhavati (…) ||
english: [She then stepped forth;] she descended into the Gārhapatya [fire]. [He who knows this] becomes a householder devoted to the household rites, a master of the house — [he who knows this].

sanskrit: (…) sāhavanīye ny akrāmat | yanty asya devā devahūtiṃ priyo devānāṃ bhavati (…) ||
english: [She then stepped forth;] she descended into the Āhavanīya [fire]. The gods come to his invocation of the gods; he becomes dear to the gods — [he who knows this].

sanskrit: (…) sā sabhāyāṃ ni (…) | yanty asya sabhāṃ sabhyo bhavati (…) ||
english: [She then stepped forth;] she descended into the assembly hall. [Men] come to his assembly; he becomes a respected member of the assembly — [he who knows this].

sanskrit: (…) sā samitau ni (…) | yanty asya samitiṃ sāmityo bhavati (…) ||
english: [She then stepped forth;] she descended into the council. [Men] come to his council; he becomes a member of authority in the council — [he who knows this].

sanskrit: (…) sāmantraṇe ny akrāmat | yanty asyāmantraṇam āmantraṇīyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: [She then stepped forth;] she descended into the deliberation. [Men] come to his deliberation; he becomes one worthy of being consulted — he who knows this.

sanskrit: (…) sāntarikṣe caturdhā vikrāntātiṣṭhat tāṃ devamanuṣyā abruvann iyaṃ tad veda yad ubhaya upajīvema- -imām upa hvāyāmahā iti tām upahvāyanta | ūrja ehi svadha ehi sūnṛta ehīrāvaty ehīti | tasyā agnir vatsa āsīd gāyatry abhidhāny abhram ūdhaḥ ||
english: [She then stepped forth;] she stood in the atmosphere striding fourfold. The gods and men said of her: 'This one knows that by which we both could live — let us call upon her.' They called upon her: 'Come, O Vigor; come, O Self-sufficiency; come, O Truth; come, O Bounty.' Of her, Agni was the calf, the Gāyatrī was the vessel over her, the cloud was the udder.

sanskrit: tasyā bṛhac ca rathantaraṃ ca dvau stanāv āstāṃ yajñāyajñiyaṃ ca vāmadevyaṃ ca dvau | oṣadhīr vai rathantaraṃ devā aduhran vyaco bṛhad apo vāmadevyaṃ yajñaṃ yajñāyajñiyam ||
english: Of her, the Bṛhat and the Rathantara were the two teats, and the Yajñāyajñiya and the Vāmadevya were the two. The Rathantara — the gods milked the plants from it; the Bṛhat — they milked wide space; the Vāmadevya — the waters; the Yajñāyajñiya — the sacrifice.

sanskrit: ete vai virājaḥ kāmadugha stanāḥ | kāmaṃkāmaṃ virājaṃ duhe ya evaṃ veda ||
english: These indeed are the wish-yielding teats of Virāj. He milks wish after wish from Virāj — he who knows this.
